translations: Fuxi put away the stone slab with the first drawing of the river map, leaving only the eight trigrams for everyone. From then on, when people encountered new changes, they no longer had to go back to the river to wait for another dragon horse, nor did they have to wait for Fuxi to redraw the trigrams. Instead, they would first observe the heavens and the earth, then distinguish between yin and yang, and finally explain their own choices. The chaotic experience thus became an understandable, verifiable, and transmissible order that could be passed down to future generations.
